wt_source: paper: Roychowdhury & Romero 2022 Cell Death Discov; Song et al. 2021 Cell Syst (PUlasso); RomeroLab/DMS-analysis C3_agg.csv
manual_evidence: coef is the positive-unlabeled logistic-regression coefficient relative to the reference residue at each position (the WT residue: all 1644 row-index letters match the WT sequence), intercept dropped, so WT = 0 by parameterisation (paper gives no number; from authors' code and the methods paper); stop rows (position-only mutant names, 77) median -0.71; per-variant se in the raw file (median 0.47) ~ half the variance of coef is estimation noise; scale is log-odds of passing a fluorescence sort (WT-to-dead range 0.7-1.0, comparable to the spread), so single-variant sign calls vs WT are unreliable (the kinetically validated activator G150R scores +1.93 with p=0.29); use se per variant

wt_source: paper: Roychowdhury & Romero 2022 Cell Death Discov; Song et al. 2021 Cell Syst (PUlasso); RomeroLab/DMS-analysis C7_agg.csv
manual_evidence: same PU-regression parameterisation as CASP3: coef is relative to the reference (WT) residue at each site, intercept dropped, so WT = 0 by construction (from the authors' code and methods paper; the caspase paper gives no number); 92 position-only rows are stop codons (index suffix '.*'), median -1.33; per-variant se in the raw file (median 0.45, Wald); scale is log-odds of passing a fluorescence sort and the substitution mass sits near +0.25 above 0, so only coef significantly > 0 (56 of 1680 at p.adj<0.05) is a defensible gain; use se per variant

wt_source: paper: Lo et al. 2023 AJHG; MaveDB urn:mavedb:00000112-a-1
manual_evidence: MaveDB: 'Variant growth scores reported relative to an arg3 deletion mutant (0) and wild type yOTC (1)'; DMS_score equals the MaveDB score (276 variants >=0.9 and 430 <0.05 match the MaveDB calibration); WT is set by construction, not a measured data point; no WT replicate SD reported (per-variant se is in MaveDB, not in ProteinGym)

wt_source: paper: Mighell et al. 2018 AJHG (Enrich2 v1.2.0 scores); PMC5986715; Rubin et al. 2017 Enrich2
manual_evidence: Scores are Enrich2 natural-log wild-type-normalised slopes ('We calculated natural log-scaled and wild-type normalized fitness scores'); null hypothesis 'behaves like wild-type (slope 0)' so WT = 0 by construction (inference from Enrich2, no numeric WT in the paper); WT-like = 95% synonymous range -1.11..0.89 (Table 1) so noise sd ~0.5; null ~ -3.4 inferred from the high-confidence variants <=-2.13 (the paper's nonsense bound) and C124S -4.9; per-variant Standard_error is in the raw file; only High_conf==1 labels are reliable

wt_source: paper: Weeks et al. 2023 Mol Biol Evol (PMC10037077) Table 1 and Methods eqs 2-4
manual_evidence: functional score = log10 of the mutant's enrichment (dim/bright sorted cells) relative to the enrichment of wild-type synonymous alleles, so WT = 0 by construction (Table 1 row 'Wild type': functional score 0); nonsense median -1.34 (RIIID nonsense -1.85 / -0.80 in the two replicas; start codon changed -2.33); WT-like noise sd ~0.05 (missense with |score|<0.1: sd 0.045, a lower bound; replica offsets ~0.05); the assay saturates above ~25% of WT activity ('buffered against about 4-fold reductions') so it measures loss only and cannot call gain; the two replicas have different scales (null -1.4..-1.8 vs -0.7..-0.8); ProteinGym's cutoff -0.055 splits the WT-like peak

wt_source: paper: Ahler et al. 2019 Mol Cell (PMC6474823); Ahler dissertation Fig 2.2A; Enrich2
manual_evidence: Activity Score = -(Enrich2 slope) of variant/WT frequency over time with 'Wild Type' normalisation, so WT = 0 by construction (dissertation Fig 2.2A: 'WT slope = 0'); the paper's Classification column defines WT-like as within +-2 SD of the mean synonymous score: loss < -0.46 < neutral < +0.63 < gain (reproduces Fig 2E counts: 403 gain / 1288 neutral / 1681 loss; neutral-class median 0.05) so noise sd ~0.27 (inferred from the class edges); stop codons median -1.606 and K298M -1.609 (dead, growth = empty vector); higher = more kinase activity = slower yeast growth (kinase is toxic in yeast); the Standard Error column is not usable as noise (70% of rows <1e-6); the raw file's 134 stop rows are not in ProteinGym

wt_source: paper: Starita et al. 2013 PNAS Dataset S1 (the 'NA-NA' no-mutation row); SI PDF
manual_evidence: Dataset S1 (98299 rows: seqID, log2_ratio, nscor_log2_ratio) has one row 'NA-NA' (no mutated positions = the wild-type U-box) with log2_ratio 0.0899 (E = 1.064), which agrees with the main-text sentence 'All E scores ... normalized to the performance of the WT U-box (E = 1.06)' (seen only as a search excerpt); WT is a measurement, 0 only within noise; ProteinGym uses the raw log2_ratio (899 of 899 singles equal Dataset S1); 33 single stop codons median -2.57 (C-terminal truncations 1168-1170 tolerated); no per-variant SE or WT replicate SD reported (technical-replicate r = 0.93); direction higher = more active
